claim: Close to 90% of Windows games launch on Linux under Proton, with the Borked tier at roughly 10%.
quote: Close to 90% of Windows games manage to launch on Linux, with the non-functional (Borked) category approaching just 10%.

claim: Of games using anti-cheat: 17% supported, 24% running, 55% broken, 4% denied; Fortnite, Valorant, Apex Legends and Rainbow Six Siege are in the Denied bucket.
RICOCHET (Call of Duty), Riot Vanguard (Valorant, League of Legends, TFT) and EA Javelin (Battlefield 6, EA Sports) do not support Linux; BattlEye, EAC and VAC do.
quote: RICOCHET, the anti-cheat used by the Call of Duty franchise and mandatory for Call of Duty: Black Ops 7, isn't supported. Riot's Vanguard doesn't support Linux, meaning titles such as League of Legends, Valorant, and Team Fight Tactics won't work.

claim: Linux browsers are limited to Widevine L3 software DRM, capping Netflix/Prime/HBO at SD-720p SDR with no HDR; HDR gaming is Wayland-only and AMD/NVIDIA-only, Intel incomplete.
quote: Linux users are restricted to Widevine L3 certification only - a software-based tier - regardless of browser choice... limited to standard definition (SD), or, best case scenario, at 720p... HDR content is simply not supported.

claim: Proton 11 entered beta in April 2026, and Proton Experimental continues shipping per-game fixes through 2026.
quote: Proton 11 Beta arrives to bring enhanced gaming compatibility to Linux / SteamOS

claim: Heroic natively supports Epic, GOG and Amazon Prime Gaming only; Battle.net/EA/Ubisoft require adding the other launcher as a non-native entry, and some publishers ban accounts running denied titles under Wine/Proton.
quote: it is possible to use the feature ADD GAME to add another store frontend like Ubisoft Connect and EA APP... some games also might ban you if you are trying to run the game on a non-supported operating system using Wine or Proton.

claim: Lutris is the launcher that integrates Battle.net, the EA app and Ubisoft Connect alongside Steam, Epic and GOG in 2026.
quote: In 2026 it integrates with Steam, Epic Games Store, GOG, Battle.net, the EA app, Ubisoft Connect, Humble Bundle, and Amazon Prime Gaming.

claim: Valve's Steam Machine launched 29 June 2026 at $1,049 for 512 GB, running SteamOS 3 (Arch-based) with a desktop mode.
quote: The Steam Machine launches June 29, 2026, starting at $1,049 for the 512 GB model... runs SteamOS 3, Valve's Arch Linux-based operating system built around the Steam client and optimized for gaming.

claim: CachyOS can deliver 5-15% higher frame rates in demanding titles versus Fedora-based distros, but reliability matters more than that delta for most users.
quote: it can deliver 5 to 15 percent higher frame rates in demanding titles compared to Fedora-based options

claim: June 2026 Steam survey Linux distro shares: SteamOS Holo 22.83%, CachyOS 14.03%, Arch 8.86%, Linux Mint 22.3 7.90%, Bazzite 7.28%.
quote: SteamOS Holo 64 bit 22.83% / CachyOS 64 bit 14.03% / Arch Linux 64 bit 8.86% / Linux Mint 22.3 64 bit 7.90% / Bazzite 64 bit 7.28%

claim: KDE Plasma 6.7.3 enables HDR gaming via a System Settings > Displays toggle (choose Color Accuracy), with gamescope for titles lacking native HDR.
quote: While there are a variety of desktops that support HDR on Linux, I'll be sticking to KDE for this demonstration. It's far easier to set up and doesn't require any configuration file tinkering.

claim: Hardware video decode on Linux uses VA-API for AMD/Intel and nvidia-vaapi-driver/NVDEC for NVIDIA, configured per-browser.
quote: HardwareVideoAcceleration - VA-API is the standard interface for hardware accelerated video decoding on Linux.
